researched.reason: Fabtech Cleanrooms Ltd (BSE SME 544332), market cap Rs 592.6 cr, close Rs 481.0 on 16-Oct-2026. Published as the order-book lane's pick. BOTH ENDS OF THE JUMP WERE RE-READ FROM THE COMPANY'S OWN MONTHLY STATEMENTS IN THIS RUN, not taken from the ledger: the filing of 10-Oct-2026 says 'As of 30 September 2026, the Company's consolidated order book stands at Rs 468.18 crore' with the segment split (Pharma 217.15, Renewable Energy 195.44, Data Centres 26.91, Semiconductors 1.99, Others 26.69), and the filing of 14-Oct-2025 says 'As of September 30, 2025, our consolidated order book stands at Rs 166.73 crore' with its own split. Same stated definition at both ends, so +180.8% YoY stands. The ratio that matters was corrected in the process: the book is 2.11x CONSOLIDATED FY26 total income of Rs 221.72 cr (FY26 deck), not 3.27x the standalone Rs 143.39 cr - the orders sit across a group whose operating weight is in Kelvin (60.50%) and the associates. WHY IT IS WORTH A CARD AND WHY CONFIDENCE IS LOW, both measured: the company publishes an order book every month with segment detail, which is rare disclosure at this size, and the book has tripled on reference wins in solar, data centres and semiconductors (the named milestone is a Rs 68 cr Waaree order). But FY26 shows what that growth cost: standalone PAT FELL 24.8% to Rs 9.06 cr, ROE went 16.64% -> 9.40%, ROCE 21.49% -> 12.08%, debt service cover 41.25x -> 0.63x as a debt-free company took on Rs 15.6 cr of bank debt, receivable turnover is 2.58x (about 141 days), and the company had to file a clarification (29-Jun-2026) that over-one-year receivables were Rs 18.32 cr 'and not 38 Crore, as referred to during the interaction' at a roadshow. Guidance is 20-40% FY27 growth with margins maintained (call of 5-May-2026); on that, the forward PE is 27-31x against 37.5x trailing consolidated - not cheap. Also on the card: 3,80,711 warrants at Rs 394 (Rs 15.00 cr, 25% paid) allotted to four non-promoters on 04-Sep-2026 after a preferential issue was withdrawn in June, and an 'Employee Leakages - information security' item in the FY26 deck.

Organic Recycling Systems Ltd (BSE SME 543997), market cap Rs 315.2 cr, close Rs 202.1 on 16-Oct-2026 (prev close Rs 201.8). Published on the filings lane. TODAY'S FILING, OPENED: its wholly owned subsidiary Solapur Bioenergy Systems secured its FIFTH 'Large-scale' EPCOM contract from BPCL in five weeks, for an organic-MSW compressed-biogas plant at Bhilai, Chhattisgarh; commissioning within 15 months of the LOA, PGTR within 18, then FIVE YEARS of O&M. The four earlier letters were opened too: Rs 85.56 cr (Mysuru) and Rs 81.73 cr (Raipur) on 08-Sep-2026, Rs 92.41 cr (Kozhikode) on 09-Sep-2026 - Rs 259.70 cr including GST, the exact cumulative figure the 09-Sep press release states - plus Hubli-Dharwad on 12-Oct-2026 and today's Bhilai, NEITHER OF WHICH CARRIES A RUPEE VALUE, only the company's 'Large-scale (Rs 50-100 crore)' band. The company puts the cumulative BPCL book at 'Rs 350-500 cr', a range, and the card says so rather than filling the gap. AGAINST A TRAILING YEAR OF SALES, as the study requires: FY26 CONSOLIDATED revenue including other income was Rs 105.68 cr (the annual report's own MD&A), so the three valued contracts ex-18% GST (about Rs 220 cr) are 2.1x a year's sales and the stated cumulative range is 2.8-4.0x - far above the 25-50% bucket the study measured, where the base rate is therefore unknown rather than better. RARITY: four prior order-type filings in the two years before today, read from the 760-day BSE list (08-Sep, 09-Sep, 12-Oct-2026 and a Madhya Pradesh CBG EPC release of 24-Feb-2026) - the middle band, not the serial-bidder band that has never produced a 5x. THE SEPARATION THAT MAKES THE VALUATION READABLE: BSE's header shows EPS Rs 3.88 and PE 52.09, both on STANDALONE PAT (Rs 4.02 cr) and a PRE-BONUS share count; on consolidated FY26 PAT of Rs 25.08 cr over the post-bonus 1,55,98,912 shares, trailing EPS is Rs 16.08 and the PE is 12.6x. RED FLAGS CARRIED ONTO THE CARD: promoters hold 15.07%; a Rs 1.69 cr service-tax demand plus an equal penalty is contested with no provision (contingent Rs 339.04 lakh); standalone receivable turnover 1.37x, about 266 days; a Rs 30 cr Bank of Baroda line to the subsidiary (corporate guarantee approved 12-Oct-2026) against Rs 300 cr-plus of EPCOM to execute; and a 23.7% consolidated PAT margin on an EPC book with no published segment P&L. Partly offsetting the promoter stake: a 10,00,000-share preferential issue at Rs 161 to promoter Mr Sarang Bhand was approved on 02-Sep-2026, though no allotment filing was found.

The Monarch Surveyors and Engineering Consultants Ltd (BSE SME 544453), market cap Rs 354.0 cr, close Rs 250.05 on 16-Oct-2026 (+4.2% on the day from Rs 240.00). TODAY'S FILING OPENED AND THE NUMBER IS GOOD: a Letter of Acceptance for traffic survey, final location survey and DPR work for new BG line, doubling and multi-tracking projects under the Chief Administrative Officer/Construction, Southern Railway, Chennai, 'total order value of the project is Rs. 51,19,56,000.29'. Against FY26 revenue of Rs 171.69 cr (BSE detailed results, audited) that is 29.8% of a trailing year of sales - squarely inside the 25-50% bucket where the 2026-09-22 study of 1,245 order filings found 2x within two years 35.7% of the time against 21.4% for orders under 10%. NOT PUBLISHED FOR ONE MEASURED REASON, THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME STUDY: Monarch is a serial order filer, decisively. Its 240-day announcement list (81 filings, status complete) contains 35 order-type filings - 'Award_of_Order_Receipt_of_Order' or 'Bagging/receiving of order(s)' - on 16-Oct, 17-Sep, 09-Sep, 03-Sep, 25-Aug, 22-Aug, 18-Aug, 14-Aug, 05-Aug, 29-Jul, 25-Jul, 20-Jul, 18-Jul (x2), 15-Jul, 11-Jul, 29-Jun, 25-Jun, 18-Jun, 12-Jun, 11-Jun, 04-Jun, 01-Jun, 18-May, 28-Apr, 27-Apr, 24-Apr and more. The study measured that a filer with eight or more prior order announcements reached 2x only 17.3% of the time and 5x NEVER, against 30.4% and 3.5% for a first-in-two-years filer. Thirty-five in eight months is four times past that threshold, so this is the bucket the method says to skip, and a Rs 51 cr LoA from a company that files one most weeks is business as usual, not a trigger. ONE THING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, flagged rather than acted on: the valuation is odd for a consultancy - BSE's header shows EPS Rs 39.59 and PE 6.32, and FY26 PAT of Rs 37.23 cr on revenue of Rs 171.69 cr is a 21.7% net margin. A 6x PE on a 21.7%-margin, asset-light engineering consultancy either prices in something the filings do not show or is a genuine mispricing; promoter holding is 72.35%, down from 98.42% at the July-2025 SME IPO. That question deserves a proper deep-dive on its own merits, not an order-filing card, and it is logged here as the reason to look again.
